purpose: Read-only repository case studies for the proposed civilization-art-design-research skill and its three design-side charters. Records what each repo demonstrates, verified license posture, pinned commit, lifecycle, and implementation lessons. No code was downloaded or executed; inspection via GitHub API (license endpoint + raw LICENSE/COPYING file reads + commit listing) on 2026-11-21.
verification: License verified by reading the LICENSE/COPYING file contents (file SHA recorded) and/or GitHub's license-detection API on 2026-11-21. 'NOASSERTION' means GitHub's classifier could not match the text — the human-read finding is given. Pinned commit = default-branch HEAD at inspection time; cite repos as URL + SHA.
bundled_note: Sanitized bundle copy of the panel inspection record; the source file of record is civilization_design_repo_cases.json in the research workspace. Case summaries: references/repo_casebook.md.

cases.name: metmuseum/openaccess

lifecycle.status: active — automated 'Open Access csv' data commits
lifecycle.note: collection CSV refreshed by Met production service

cases.demonstrates: A major museum publishing its collection metadata as CC0 data: every object record carries accession number, credit line, and rights field. Anchor fixture for the provenance lab (L6) and for Robins-canon figure lab (L3) image sourcing.
implementation_lessons: CC0 applies to the metadata and to designated open-access images; the per-record 'Rights and Reproduction' field still controls individual works — always read the record, never assume.
Data snapshots are moving: pin the CSV commit SHA in any research artifact that cites object records.
Accession number + objectURL is the citation unit; images may additionally carry photographer/museum policy terms.

cases.name: Smithsonian/OpenAccess

lifecycle.status: static README/metadata hub — underlying data releases live on Smithsonian's S3 infrastructure, not in this repo

cases.demonstrates: CC0 release at federal-institution scale (4.5M+ images/data), with usage guidance that still requests attribution and flags third-party rights in some assets.
implementation_lessons: Repo stillness is not dataset stillness: check the live metadata API/bulk data date, not the GitHub README, for currency.
Smithsonian's own usage terms ask users to verify per-item rights for content not created by the Smithsonian — a CC0 umbrella does not launder embedded third-party rights.
Good negative-example for lifecycle checks: an unmaintained-looking repo can front a maintained dataset.

cases.name: IIIF/api

license.spdx: no repo-level LICENSE file (verified at root listing 2026-11-21); IIIF specifications are published under open terms on iiif.io — record per-specification notice when excerpting
license.how_verified: root directory listing — no LICENSE/COPYING file

lifecycle.status: active — community-driven spec development (Image API, Presentation API)

cases.demonstrates: Interoperable image delivery for cultural heritage: deep-zoom pixels (Image API) and object structure/annotations (Presentation API) as inspectable, versioned specifications; the standard plumbing for museum-image labs.
implementation_lessons: Cite IIIF specs by API name + version (e.g., Image API 3.0); manifests are JSON-LD and validate against published schemas.
Absence of a LICENSE file is itself a finding: record it, then check the consortium site terms before republishing spec text.
info.json capability introspection lets tooling adapt to what a given server supports — don't hardcode server behavior.

cases.name: isohedral/tactile

lifecycle.status: stable/dormant — last default-branch commit 2022; author Craig S. Kaplan's research continues via papers and other ports (tactile-python/tactile-rs/tactile-cs forks observed in search, not inspected)

cases.demonstrates: Reference implementation of the 93 isohedral tiling types (Grünbaum–Shephard incidence symbols): the computation backbone for modern tiling labs; also Kaplan's own attribution practice for pattern-generation research.
implementation_lessons: Dormant + permissive license = safe to pin and read; treat algorithmic claims against the Grünbaum–Shephard reference, not against the repo.
The IH-type system is a modern classification (1987); teaching materials must not attribute it to historical pattern-makers.
BSD-3-Clause requires retaining the notice — put it in the lab's NOTICE file, not just a comment.

cases.name: paperjs/paper.js

license.spdx: MIT (GitHub: NOASSERTION due to custom preamble; LICENSE.txt is verbatim MIT text)

cases.demonstrates: Scriptable vector graphics with boolean path operations and SVG import/export — the practical substrate for browser-side ornament/pattern labs without a server.
implementation_lessons: NOASSERTION is not a license problem by itself: read the file; here it is verbatim MIT with a preamble.
Boolean path ops are floating-point: lab acceptance tests need tolerance declarations (coordinate with computational-geometry-engineering).
SVG export preserves authored structure only if the author structures groups/ids deliberately — teach semantic grouping in pattern labs.

cases.name: openscad/openscad

license.spdx: GPL-2.0-only with explicit CGAL linking exception (COPYING preamble)

cases.demonstrates: Code-as-CAD: fully parametric, diff-able solid models — the right host for Roriczer/stepwell construction labs where every geometric step must be inspectable text.
implementation_lessons: GPL-2.0 covers the application; user .scad models are user works (running output), but bundling OpenSCAD into a distributed product triggers copyleft — record this distinction in delivery reviews.
CGAL dependency explains the linking exception; downstream license audits must include transitive libraries.
Deterministic CSG makes it ideal for 'construction closes within declared tolerance' acceptance tests (lab L4).

cases.name: FreeCAD/FreeCAD

lifecycle.status: active — large multi-workbench project (note: repo contains AGENTS.md and AI_POLICY.md; agent-authored contributions are policy-governed)

cases.demonstrates: Full parametric B-rep CAD (Open CASCADE kernel) with Python console: constraint-sketch workflows for the documented-procedure labs; also a governance example (published AI-contribution policy).
implementation_lessons: LGPL-2.1 permits linking but modified-library distribution carries source obligations; plugin authors stay permissive, core contributors follow the project license.
FreeCAD files (.FCStd) are zip containers — provenance labs can inspect document.xml for parameter history.
Its AGENTS.md/AI_POLICY.md is a model citation when drafting agent-contribution rules for creative toolchains.

cases.name: antiprism/antiprism

license.spdx: NOASSERTION — Debian-format COPYING declares 'MIT-and-similar, permissive with attribution' for the bulk of files; check per-file notes
license.how_verified: COPYING file read via license API

cases.demonstrates: Command-line polyhedron/off-file toolkit (uniform polyhedra, symmetry operations, geodesics) — useful for ornament-to-solid exercises and for teaching polyhedral symmetry beyond the plane groups.
implementation_lessons: Debian-format copyright files encode per-file license variation — audit at file granularity before excerpting.
Maintenance-mode CLI tools are stable fixtures: pin the commit, record build-toolchain versions if ever compiled.
OFF is a teachable minimal mesh format; conversions to it must declare handedness/units (coordinate with computational-geometry-engineering).
